title: Time-resolved ARPES in pumped excitonic systems: Floquet physics induced by excitonic fields
abstract: We develop a theoretical framework based on the Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach (DPOA) to study the time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) of pumped excitonic systems. Including Coulomb electron-electron interactions at the Hartree-Fock (HF) level, our formalism captures the formation of excitonic bound states under the application of pump pulses. Considering a prototypical two-dimensional two-band semiconductor, we analyze the equilibrium phase diagram, which shows the expected transition from a semiconducting to an excitonic-insulator phase as the Coulomb interaction strength or its range increase. Out of equilibrium, we find that when the pump frequency is resonant with an excitonic mode, coherent oscillations of the excitonic order parameter persist after the pump pulse subsides and give rise to clear Floquet sidebands in the TR-ARPES spectrum. These exciton-field-induced sidebands are distinct from those originating from the pump laser field. We also identify band-resonance-induced sidebands arising from residual coherences at momenta where the band gap is resonant with the pump frequency. Finally, we analyze the local Coulomb interaction limit. Our results corroborate recent experimental observations of exciton-field-induced Floquet-like sidebands and establish DPOA as an efficient and accurate method for simulating ultrafast phenomena in interacting electron systems.
summary: The paper develops a sophisticated theoretical framework using the Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach to simulate how excitonic systems behave under intense, time-varying pump pulses. By including electron-electron interactions via Hartree-Fock theory, the authors predict and analyze distinct Floquet sidebands arising from coherent oscillations of the internal excitonic order parameter. This work provides a powerful tool for interpreting ultrafast spectroscopic measurements in correlated materials.
main_problem: The study focuses on understanding time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) in excitonic systems subjected to external pumping fields, specifically investigating Floquet physics induced by internal excitonic coherence.
main_result: The authors show that when the pump frequency matches an excitonic mode, coherent oscillations persist after the pulse, generating distinct Floquet sidebands unique to the excitonic field. They also establish DPOA as a robust method for simulating these ultrafast dynamics.
method: The theoretical framework utilizes the Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach (DPOA) combined with the Hartree-Fock approximation to treat Coulomb electron-electron interactions in an out-of-equilibrium setting.
model_or_system: The model is a prototypical two-dimensional, two-band semiconductor system. The Hamiltonian includes non-interacting terms and a Coulomb interaction term treated via HF decoupling, allowing for the study of excitonic bound states formation.
key_observables: TR-ARPES spectrum; excitonic order parameter oscillations; Floquet sidebands (distinguishing between pump-field vs. exciton-field origin); equilibrium phase diagram.
important_parameters: Coulomb interaction strength/range; pump frequency resonance with an excitonic mode; dipole asymmetry ($D$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations are the use of the Hartree-Fock (HF) approximation for Coulomb interactions and solving the time evolution using DPOA.
figures_summary: Figure 8 compares post-pump TR-ARPES signals at the $\Gamma$ point, demonstrating that dipole asymmetry ($D$) is crucial for observing exciton-field-induced Floquet sidebands in both semiconducting and excitonic-insulator phases.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first introducing the theoretical necessity of studying TR-ARPES in pumped systems. It then details the DPOA formalism, extending it to include HF interactions to model exciton formation and subsequent out-of-equilibrium dynamics under resonant pumping conditions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it models non-equilibrium many-body physics (excitons) driven by time-dependent fields (pumping), generating characteristic Floquet signatures that can be measured experimentally. The use of DPOA for ultrafast correlation effects is a key theoretical contribution.
